9.0.s.en: 1. Man's inability to know God's purposes:

9.0.0.en: 1 For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God: no man knoweth either love or hatred by all that is before them. 2 All things come alike to all: there is one event to the righteous, and to the wicked; to the good and to the clean, and to the unclean; to him that sacrificeth, and to him that sacrificeth not: as is the good, so is the sinner; and he that sweareth, as he that feareth an oath. 3 This is an evil among all things that are done under the sun, that there is one event unto all: yea, also the heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live, and after that they go to the dead.

9.0.1.en: "For all this I considered in my heart even to declare all this, that the righteous, and the wise, and their works, are in the hand of God:

9.0.2.en: no man knoweth either love or hatred by all that is before them" [1].

9.0.3.en: * The meaning is that I have given my heart to contemplation, longing to know whom the Lord loves and whom He hates. And I found in truth that the works of the righteous are in the hand of God, but as to whether they are loved or hated by God, they waver, not being certain of it.

9.0.4.en: St. Jerome The obscurity of the text raises many questions, among them: how is it that the believer does not know whether he is loved by God or not? And does God hate anyone?

9.0.5.en: What the Preacher affirms is that all the righteous and the wise, with all their works, are in the hand of God, whether their days are full of joy or of sorrow and troubles... It is not fitting for the true believer to doubt God's providence for him and His care for all his affairs, small and great. But man in his weakness stands wavering, asking: Does God love him or hate him? In the bitterness of affliction thoughts pass through him to crush him: that God is taking vengeance on him, or hates him, or does not feel his weaknesses. For this he often asks: Why does God permit me harsh trials that almost crush my spirit and make me lose my faith?

9.1.0.en: Perhaps what causes some to stumble is that they see no difference between what befalls the righteous and the wicked, the good and the bad, the clean and the unclean, him that sacrificeth (offers a sacrifice to God) and him that sacrificeth not, him that sweareth (falsely) and him that feareth an oath... so that in their astonishment and confusion they become like those in a state of madness [2-3], not knowing the interpretation of the events that befall them and those around them.

9.1.1.en: In truth, even though the life of the righteous and all their works are in the hand of God, it is difficult for the natural man to perceive this because of the similarity of outward circumstances for the righteous and the wicked, the wise and the foolish, and it is dangerous to measure God's love for us by outward circumstances.

9.1.2.en: Would that we were not preoccupied with outward events but looked into our depths to see the hand of God at work establishing His Kingdom in us, and saw Him setting up the icon of His heavens in us, so that we rejoice and exult, and He also rejoices in us when He sees us as His little children who perceive His wisdom and enjoy it, as the Evangelist says: "Jesus rejoiced in spirit and said: I thank You, O Father... because You have hid these things from the wise and revealed them unto babes" (Mt 11:25). He rejoices in the little children who are prepared by His heavenly revelation and His wisdom for the eternal wedding feast.

9.1.3.en: * Alas for the frailty and passing of human nature! Yet our faith in Christ lifts us to heaven and promises us the eternity of our souls. As for material conditions in life, they are the same for us and for the beasts also.

9.2.s.en: 2. God gives us opportunities for repentance:

9.2.0.en: 4 For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion. 5 For the living know that they shall die: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten. 6 Also their love, and their hatred, and their envy, is now perished; neither have they any more a portion for ever in any thing that is done under the sun.

9.2.1.en: What grieves the heart of the Preacher is that God gives man opportunities for repentance in this life, so that he may return to himself and contemplate God's dealings with him instead of being confused by the outward events that crush his spirit, but instead of benefiting from them his heart is filled with evil and folly until death overtakes him suddenly.

9.2.2.en: The wise Solomon compares the living and the dead, making clear the following:

9.3.s.en: a. The living man, for whose repentance we hope:

9.3.0.en: As for the dead man, he has lost the opportunity of repentance: "For to him that is joined to all the living there is hope: for a living dog is better than a dead lion" [4]. If a man reaches such uncleanness that he is called a "dog" - for dogs in the Old Testament were among the unclean animals much hated by them, so that they called the pagan Gentiles by this name - he is better than a dead lion.

9.3.1.en: A man may look upon himself as a dog because of his many weaknesses and falls, but in a spirit of humility he gains new life and becomes better than the one who prides himself on his own righteousness, counting himself a lion, for by pride he has become dead!

9.3.2.en: * Many of the righteous have fallen from their righteousness, and many sinners have taken their place; therefore it is not fitting for the righteous man to exalt himself, for he is still in the flesh, nor is it fitting for the sinner to despair, for God is near to him if he seeks Him, and is ready to receive him if he changes his way of life and turns to (the Lord).

9.3.3.en: St. Isaac the Syrian A man of few gifts, if he thinks in himself that he has no part in life and no authority or power, like a despised dog (in the eyes of the Jews), when he is united with the living Christ, risen from the dead, becomes better than one who has many gifts and abilities, and temporal glory and majesty like the lion, but who, by withdrawing from his Savior, loses his life and is counted dead! Our life is in Christ, and our resurrection through Him is better than every ability or greatness!

9.4.s.en: b. The living man who is sincere with himself prepares for the day of his departure:

9.4.0.en: "For the living know that they shall die:

9.5.0.en: but the dead know not any thing, neither have they any more a reward; for the memory of them is forgotten" [5].

9.6.0.en: Every human being is aware of this truth, that he will surely die... But the living man who is careful for the salvation of his soul and concerned for his eternity enjoys an effective knowledge that drives him to prepare for that day, whereas he who has died without repentance no longer has knowledge, because he has really died and has no return to life here to strive and receive a reward, but he and all his works have come into the realm of oblivion. Where has his love of the world gone? Where is his hatred of others and his envy of them? All this has perished with him, and neither he nor his works have a portion in eternal life [6].

9.7.s.en: 3. Let us work for the eternal wedding feast:

9.7.0.en: 7 Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works. 8 Let thy garments be always white; and let thy head lack no ointment. 9 Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun. 10 Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.

9.7.1.en: If death closes the door of repentance completely, and man loses all that he gathered in this life as long as he is outside the circle of the Lord, then it befits us to work while we are alive; to work in the spirit of divine wisdom to prepare for the eternal wedding feast. The Preacher offered the following counsels:

9.8.s.en: a. Let us live our lives with joy, with a good heart:

9.8.0.en: "Go thy way, eat thy bread with joy, and drink thy wine with a merry heart; for God now accepteth thy works" [7].

9.8.1.en: The Preacher often repeats our duty to use God's gifts, even the temporal ones, with spiritual joy and a spirit of thanksgiving to God... Let us eat, drink and work in a spirit of moderation. "Whether therefore ye eat, or drink, or whatsoever ye do, do all to the glory of God" (1 Cor 10:31).

9.8.2.en: The life of joy here amid sufferings prepares the soul for eternal joy, where there is no affliction or pain but constant joy and a wedding feast that never ends.

9.9.s.en: b. Let us enjoy the heavenly feast:

9.9.0.en: The Bridegroom offers us His Body as bread that gladdens the soul and His Blood as wine that cheers it... and through this wondrous sacrament He abides in us and we in Him, so we are counted the object of the Father's pleasure, and He is pleased with all our works.

9.9.1.en: * Solomon, referring to that grace, says in the book of Ecclesiastes: "Come, eat thy bread with joy" - of course the spiritual bread - "Come" is a joyful call to salvation and blessing.

9.9.2.en: "And drink thy wine with a merry heart (with a joyful soul)," that is, the spiritual wine.

9.9.3.en: "And pour oil upon thy head." Here you see how he points to the mystical anointing.

9.9.4.en: "Let thy garments be always white; for God now accepteth thy works" [7-8]. Now that you have put off your old garments and put on spiritual white, you must keep your garments always white. I do not mean that you must always wear white clothes, but that you must be clothed in true purity and spiritual radiance, so that you may say with the blessed Isaiah: "My soul shall be joyful in my God; for he hath clothed me with the garments of salvation, he hath covered me with the robe of gladness" (Isa 61:10).

9.9.5.en: St. Cyril of Jerusalem And it is wonderful that when the Lord Christ offers us His Body and Blood, given for us as a joyful food that prepares us for the eternal wedding feast through our union with Him, He calls them "thy bread" and "thy wine." He has become our possession, so they are counted our bread and our wine, indeed in an intimate personal relationship, as being my bread and my wine!

9.9.6.en: Whenever we enjoy the service of the Eucharist (the Divine Liturgy), we realize that we are receiving the pledge of the eternal wedding feast and the heavenly banquet; we feel an inner rejoicing of heart, and God's longing and His pleasure in us in Christ Jesus, the Bridegroom of our souls. We put on our Christ as a robe of righteousness that removes our nakedness and takes away our shortcomings, and we enjoy His splendor upon us.

9.9.7.en: Let us take care to put on the wedding garment here, so that we may not be deprived of the wedding feast and union with our Bridegroom.

9.9.8.en: * I have often praised the virgins, widows and married women who have kept their garments always white, who follow the Lamb whithersoever He goeth.

9.9.9.en: * We are told that the Bridegroom feeds among the lilies, that is, among those who have not defiled their garments, for they have remained virgins (spiritually), and have listened to the Preacher's saying: "Let thy garments be always white."

9.9.10.en: * He who does not have the wedding garment and has not kept that commandment, "Let thy garments be always white," is bound hand and foot, so he does not know how to recline at the table or sit on a throne or stand at the right hand of God, but is cast into Gehenna, where there is wailing and gnashing of teeth.

9.10.s.en: c. Family warmth, a pledge of heavenly love:

9.10.0.en: The spiritual man sees in his holy family life a living image of the heavenly family; the family love he practices extends into heaven as an eternal love...

9.11.0.en: "Live joyfully with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of the life of thy vanity, which he hath given thee under the sun, all the days of thy vanity: for that is thy portion in this life, and in thy labour which thou takest under the sun" [9].

9.11.1.en: It befits the married believer to practice his married life with sincere love, counting his marriage a divine gift... Truly the life he lives is short and passing, so that those who marry are as though they did not marry, but it is God's gift that man lives, that he may hear the voice that says: "Thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things" (Mt 25:21, 23; Lk 19:17)... His short life is his portion from the Lord, bearing many troubles because it is a life "under the sun," but his faithfulness in it lifts him up to a life of everlasting wedding feast above the sun, in which he finds no weariness.

9.12.0.en: "Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest" [10].

9.12.1.en: As long as we have not yet departed to the tomb (perhaps by the grave he meant the tomb), it befits us to strive earnestly with all our strength so that we may enjoy spiritual knowledge and heavenly wisdom, and be made worthy of the heavenly wedding feast. Let us bear the Cross here, and we shall enjoy the everlasting feast of the Resurrection.

9.12.2.en: * The way of the Lord is a daily cross; no one ascends to heaven in ease (comfort), for we know where the way of comfort leads and where it ends.

9.12.3.en: St. Isaac the Syrian * Grace is always ready! It seeks those who receive it with all welcome. So when our Lord sees a soul that is watchful and aflame with love, He pours out His riches upon it in abundance and plenty above all its requests.

9.12.4.en: * Be sure that it is impossible for a man to put forth all his effort to be saved, and do all that is in his power, and God leave him.

9.12.5.en: St. John Chrysostom * If you grieve (in striving) in seeking Him, you will rejoice in His presence!

9.12.6.en: * He who is diligent and seeks finds, and he who is slothful remains in blindness, in the outer darkness with the people of the left hand like himself.

9.12.7.en: * Work diligently, and you will see the tree of life blossom in the midst of your paradise.

9.13.s.en: 4. Work is of no avail without grace:

9.13.0.en: 11 I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all.

9.13.1.en: When the Preacher calls us to daily striving to prepare for the eternal wedding feast, he affirms that our striving is of no avail unless God works in us.

9.13.2.en: "I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favour to men of skill; but time and chance happeneth to them all" [11].

9.13.3.en: So if a man attains success in his running, he relies on God and not on the lightness of his body; in his struggle against sin he depends on the grace of God and not on his own strength and righteousness; in his success in practical life he does not obtain his bread by human wisdom but by God's providence for him; the wealth he enjoys does not rest on his own understanding but on the blessing of the Lord; and the favour he has in the eyes of men is not due to his knowledge and learning... For an entire army fled before Jonathan and his armourbearer (1 Sam 14:12-15). As it is said: "One man of you shall chase a thousand: for the LORD your God, he it is that fighteth for you" (Josh 23:10). God is the secret of our success, our victory, our satisfaction, our wealth and our wisdom.

9.13.4.en: * However much you hasten in running, and however much you multiply your struggles, you need One to give you the crown. "Except the LORD build the house, they labour in vain that build it: except the LORD keep the city, the watchman waketh but in vain." And he says that I know that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, nor victory to the fighters, nor the harbors of safety to the valiant soldiers, but victory belongs to God, and to Him belongs the reaching of the safety of righteousness.

9.13.5.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus * The man who doubts that God helps him in good work is like one who flees from his shadow, and he suffers in time of luxury and wealth and is tempted in time of ease, and affliction comes upon him! But he who puts his trust in God is steadfast of heart, and proclaims his worthiness to all men, and his praise comes before the face of his enemies.

9.13.6.en: * No man can obtain spiritual knowledge unless he changes and becomes like a little child.

9.13.7.en: St. Isaac the Syrian * We cannot run in the way of God unless we are carried on the wings of the Spirit.

9.13.8.en: * None is stronger than he who enjoys heavenly help, as none is weaker than he who is deprived of it.

9.13.9.en: St. John Chrysostom When the Preacher calls us to striving that rests on God's free grace, he affirms to us the necessity of our readiness at any moment, because we do not know the times and seasons, for he says: "Time and chance happeneth to them all," or "the hour and events come upon them suddenly" [11].

9.14.0.en: 12 For man also knoweth not his time: as the fishes that are taken in an evil net, and as the birds that are caught in the snare; so are the sons of men snared in an evil time, when it falleth suddenly upon them. 13 This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it seemed great unto me: 14 There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it: 15 Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city; yet no man remembered that same poor man. 16 Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength: nevertheless the poor man's wisdom is despised, and his words are not heard. 17 The words of wise men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools. 18 Wisdom is better than weapons of war: but one sinner destroyeth much good.

9.14.1.en: Man does not know what time may bring upon him by surprise, for he is like the fish that may rejoice in food offered to it and finds itself in a net, and like the bird that finds itself caught in a snare [12]. We do not know what troubles await us and what the day offers us... Our souls may be required, we may bear some trial, and we may enjoy relief!

9.15.0.en: Our weapon before time, with all the joys and troubles it carries, is true wisdom: "This wisdom have I seen also under the sun, and it seemed great unto me" [13]. He means here the wisdom that enables a man who loves his country and mankind - at the expense of his personal comfort - to deliver his city from imminent danger, from an army besieging it... and in this he does not ask for a word of praise!

9.15.1.en: "There was a little city, and few men within it; and there came a great king against it, and besieged it, and built great bulwarks against it:

9.15.2.en: Now there was found in it a poor wise man, and he by his wisdom delivered the city;

9.16.0.en: yet no man remembered that same poor man" [14-15].

9.16.1.en: What is this city but man, who carries powers and potentials of soul and body, of emotions, feelings, mind, gifts, and so on... He is like a little city with few men within it, and the devil is like a great king besieging it, for with all the devil's mighty capacities he covets man, wanting to snatch him from the hand of God to join him to his kingdom, and to subject him for his own account, insulting him and tormenting him as one taking vengeance on him. He builds great bulwarks against him to ruin him, since he wishes to establish his kingdom in him and make of him a battlefield against good... Before this might man fears and trembles, at one time for the sake of material gain, at another for pride, at a third as a kind of surrender, and so on... But the poor wise man who delivers the city by his wisdom is the Lord Christ, who emptied Himself and took our nature, and offered us His Cross to declare that His weakness is stronger than strength, and His poverty richer than all riches! Yet no one remembers this man, for all forsook Him at the Cross... He became, in the shame of the Cross, outside the camp! He came unto His own, and His own received Him not.

9.16.2.en: So let us possess our Christ, the true "Wisdom," for it is said: "Then said I, Wisdom is better than strength." The devil is strong, and sin is exceedingly sinful, but the wisdom of Christ overcomes them. Yet we must distinguish between constructive heavenly wisdom and entanglement in the philosophies of the world if they conflict with the life of faith. St. Basil the Great says:

9.16.3.en: [I have wasted much time in vanity, and spent most of my youth in the empty labor to which I devoted myself, learning the teaching of a wisdom that God has made foolish (1 Cor 1:20), until the day came when, as though I had awakened from a deep sleep, I looked upon the brilliant light of the truth in the Gospel and saw the vanity of the wisdom of the princes of this world, that come to nought (1 Cor 2:6). Then I wept over my wretched life].

9.16.4.en: If the devil, with his works of evil and with death, is like the cry of a strong man who ruleth among fools, yet the quiet of the wise Christ is greater... He came not crying out, and no one heard His voice, and behold He shatters the violent cries of the enemy, giving us His own Spirit that we may overcome by quiet wisdom.

9.17.0.en: "The words of wise men are heard in quiet more than the cry of him that ruleth among fools. Wisdom is better than weapons of war" [17-18].

9.18.0.en: Let us be united with the Lord Christ, the Giver of victory against the devil who rules, and let us also lessen friendship with the wicked lest they corrupt our fellowship with the Lord Christ. "But one sinner destroyeth much good" [18].
